title: Resolve fragment splice ambiguity and toolcall handoff
author: Lina Chen
release_notes: Fixes an intermittent streaming parser bug where message fragments split across TCP/HTTP chunk boundaries could produce malformed JSON or reorder function/tool-call sentinel events. Improves reassembly heuristics and adds defensive checks to avoid toolcall misdelivery. No API contract changes.
description:
Context: Several customers and internal canaries reported intermittent failures when using the OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoint: partial JSON payloads or tool/function call sentinel events arriving out of order after network fragmentation or aggressive proxy chunking. The root cause is ambiguous fragment splice handling in the streaming parser: when a JSON boundary or toolcall sentinel sits on a chunk boundary, the previous reassembly logic would sometimes accept a premature end or delay a toolcall event, causing malformed JSON or function-call ordering regressions.

Motivation: Robustness of the streaming API is critical for downstream SDKs and tool call semantics. This change tightens the streaming reassembly window and introduces explicit boundary anchoring heuristics so event boundaries are preserved even when fragments arrive split or reordered by intermediate layers. It also avoids reconstructing partial JSON strings across non-deterministic chunk cuts without verification.

What I changed (high level):
- Introduced a FragmentAnchor table keyed by stream-id + monotonically-increasing span-id to detect and reconcile overlapping fragment ranges.
- Added an idempotent reassembly pass that validates JSON/bracket depth and string literal state before emitting a completed message. If ambiguity remains, we delay emission until a checksum or sentinel frames the span.
- Added sentinel-level ordering guarantees for tool/function-call handoff: toolcall events are now emitted only after their complete argument span is validated and reassembled; we add a short ack-window to ensure downstream router has accepted the previous fragment when applicable.
- Tightened delimiter handling: the parser no longer treats consecutive newlines as an atomic event boundary when inside a JSON string or unclosed brace/array; it now consults depth and escape-state to decide.
- Implemented end-to-end tests and a new fuzz harness simulating chunk reordering, CRLF/\n splits, and mid-utf8 boundary cuts.
- Added regression tests that reproduce customer canary failures and assert stable ordering of toolcall events.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for fragment reassembly and delimiter heuristics
- [x] Fuzz tests for chunk reordering and mid-codepoint splits
- [x] Integration tests covering function/tool call sequences over streaming API
- [x] Benchmarked (no measurable latency regression on typical workloads)
- [x] Docs note for compatibility layer changes (internal)

Commits (summary):
- 7f2c3d1: introduce FragmentAnchor and reassembly state machine; core parser hooks
- b3a1f5e: add checksum guard and sentinel ack window for toolcall handoff
- c4d2a9b: tighten delimiter logic to consult depth and escape state
- e8f7c11: integration tests reproducing reported canary failure; add fuzz harness
- 9aabb33: small refactor and error message improvements; add metrics for reassembly requeues

Files changed (high level):
- internal/streaming/parser/reassembly.go (new logic for fragment anchoring and checksum guards)
- internal/streaming/parser/delimiter.go (depth/escape-aware delimiter handling)
- internal/streaming/handshake/toolhandoff.go (ack-window and ordering guards for toolcall events)
- sdk/openai_compat/streaming_integration_test.go (integration reproduction tests)
- test/fuzz/chunk_reorder_fuzz.go (fuzz harness)
- telemetry/metrics/reassembly_metrics.yaml (new metrics)
- docs/internal/compat/streaming-frag-reassembly.md (design notes)
- Makefile / CI config tweaks to run fuzz target in nightly jobs

Small illustrative snippet (parser guard):
- Previously: emit on double-newline unconditionally
- Now: if depth != 0 or in_string == true then buffer until validated by checksum/sentinel

Review conversation (high level):
- Miguel: "Can we avoid increasing latency for small messages?"
  - Lina: "Microbenchmarked the common path; if fragments are complete the fast-path short-circuits and emission cost is unchanged. Only ambiguous cases hit the new verification window."
- Ravi: "What about proxies that re-chunk aggressively and reorder? Any state explosion risk?"
  - Lina: "FragmentAnchor coalesces adjacent spans and we cap anchor table size per-stream; we also emit a metric when we evict anchors to trigger investigation rather than silently failing."
- Aisha: "Add a test for a 3-way out-of-order reassembly where toolcall lands ahead of content."
  - Lina: "Added test 'TestToolcallOrderingThreeWay' to integration suite; it asserts stable ordering and that no toolcall is applied without its payload."

CI & Stability: Initial CI run surfaced a flaky fuzz target (timeout) that caused a rerun. After increasing the timeout and a small harness fix the full CI run passed (unit, integration, lint, format, fuzz-nightly). The changelist also adds a nightly fuzz job to track regressions.

Merge outcome: Merged to main via squash merge on 2025-02-13 after approval from reviewers and CI passing. No manual rollbacks required; canary rollout to hosted API showed no errors in 48h window.

Notes for SDK teams: The OpenAI-compat streaming semantics are preserved at the API level, but SDKs should observe the new ordering guarantees (toolcall events will not be emitted until validated). This is backward-compatible but may change the interleaving timing in pathological proxy cases; we've added notes to internal SDK release checklists.

Follow-ups (open items):
- Monitor new metrics (reassembly.evictions, reassembly.requeues) for two weeks and create alerts if rates climb above threshold.
- Consider exposing a diagnostic header in the streaming response for high-sensitivity customers to help debug reassembly failures in the field.

References: ENG-5432 (bug triage), ENG-5460 (streaming reliability epic), internal canary incident #INC-2025-01-28-07
